engineering-tests-wait-on-stateengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passThe suite that drives a browser is set in vitest.browser.config.ts (include &#39;tests/browser/**/*.test.ts&#39;). That glob matches exactly three files: inspect.int.test.ts, verify.e2e.test.ts and bootstrap.int.test.ts. helpers.ts is their shared module. The unit config runs tests/unit under jsdom and does not drive a real browser. I quote all four browser files in full, and none of them sleeps for a fixed time or uses an immediately-returning call as a wait. (1) inspect.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits runNpm subprocess runs. The only direct Playwright test, &#39;captures only after the transition settles&#39;, awaits chromium.launch, page.setContent and page.evaluate, and the evaluate awaits img.decode(). It then asserts on pixel counts that have already been computed. The remaining tests assert on PNG files and output that the completed runs produced. (2) verify.e2e.test.ts: every test awaits runNpm and then asserts on the finished process&#39;s output and exit code. previewIsGone is a fetch bounded by AbortSignal.timeout. The only setTimeout in the file is in-page app code that a fault case injects into Scene.tsx. (3) bootstrap.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits spawnSync and runNpm, and the tests assert on their results and on file contents. (4) helpers.ts: runNpm resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event. Its setTimeout is only a SIGKILL safeguard for a hung child, not a wait before an assertion. Inside the scripts, step changes are awaited by polling: waitForStepIndex calls page.waitForFunction on data-step-index with a timeout. Judge C&#39;s fail rests on page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) at scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:50. That call is in the delivered inspect helper, not in a test. The helper reaches it only after waitForStepIndex has confirmed the step (line 45), so the test&#39;s step assertions are not waiting on a sleep. The settle delay is a product option (--settle-ms) that the test exercises: it compares default-delay captures with --settle-ms 0 captures. The test does not use it to time its own assertions. The criterion is about how the browser tests wait, and the guidance excludes settle-delay length from scoring. When an existing package.json is present, `plan.addDependencies` etc. are merged, but the lockfile is never copied or updated, and `npm install` in the CLI runs unconstrained. Separately, in the `plan.createPackage` branch, `name: path.basename(resolved.target)` can produce an invalid npm package name (e.g. uppercase or spaces in the directory name), which makes `npm install`/`npm ci` fail with an unclear error after files were already written.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib/preview.mjs:121 In startPreview, when the child process exits early the loop throws PhaseError without anything else needed, but if `fetch` hangs (no timeout), the 30s deadline check is never reached because the await never resolves. A port accepted by another process that never responds stalls verify/inspect indefinitely, and on that path the preview child is never stopped by startPreview (callers only get `preview` after it returns).\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:23 `readRegistry(root)` is called with a regex-based parser and the slug is then interpolated into the URL. More importantly, `waitForStepIndex(page, index)` is awaited with default 5s timeout and failures propagate as a generic Playwright timeout message, without naming the step; the inspect run also never attaches console/pageerror listeners, so a presentation that crashes mid-way yields only a timeout error and the already-captured screenshots give no hint.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib/diagnostics.mjs:108 `indistinct()` builds `modal` from `[...tally.entries()].sort(...)`, and `sameSignature(chrome.active, JSON.parse(modal[0]))` compares only keys of `active`. SKILL.md directs a full scaffold of an empty directory without asking, and says `apply` installs the dependencies and that none may be assumed installed. The bootstrap template contains all three anchors: build config, `src/presentation-kit/` and `src/presentations/index.ts` with Root and route. Its package.json lists react, react-dom, motion, lucide-react, vite, plugin-react, typescript with its types, the ESLint stack and playwright. `bootstrap.mjs` `applyScaffold` copies the files and the CLI then runs `npm install`. The test INT-001 in bootstrap.int.test.ts materializes the template into a fresh temp dir via `apply --dir &lt;tmp&gt; --no-install` from an unrelated cwd. consensus{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","basis":"consensus-pass","votes":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","rationale":"Talk.tsx renders the kit&#39;s Presentation with the STEPS array, title, className and initialMode, so the kit handles navigation, chrome and stage. It calls checkSample.registered for each expectation. scripts/lib/sample-check.mjs (lines 5-11) returns an explicit message when the slug is not registered or its title differs. main() throws that as PhaseError(&#39;sample&#39;). 2. **Steps missing or out of order.** renderPresentation compares the reported step count with the expected count (verify.mjs lines 41-44, sample-check.mjs lines 13-16). A missing or non-numeric step count becomes 0 or NaN, which never equals the expected count, so it cannot pass. For each step, the era, title and caption are compared with the expected values for that index (verify.mjs lines 58-65, sample-check.mjs lines 18-27). I quote all four browser files in full, and none of them sleeps for a fixed time or uses an immediately-returning call as a wait. (1) inspect.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits runNpm subprocess runs. The only direct Playwright test, &#39;captures only after the transition settles&#39;, awaits chromium.launch, page.setContent and page.evaluate, and the evaluate awaits img.decode(). It then asserts on pixel counts that have already been computed. The remaining tests assert on PNG files and output that the completed runs produced. (2) verify.e2e.test.ts: every test awaits runNpm and then asserts on the finished process&#39;s output and exit code. previewIsGone is a fetch bounded by AbortSignal.timeout. The only setTimeout in the file is in-page app code that a fault case injects into Scene.tsx. (3) bootstrap.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits spawnSync and runNpm, and the tests assert on their results and on file contents. (4) helpers.ts: runNpm resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event. Its setTimeout is only a SIGKILL safeguard for a hung child, not a wait before an assertion. Inside the scripts, step changes are awaited by polling: waitForStepIndex calls page.waitForFunction on data-step-index with a timeout. Judge C&#39;s fail rests on page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) at scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:50. That call is in the delivered inspect helper, not in a test. The helper reaches it only after waitForStepIndex has confirmed the step (line 45), so the test&#39;s step assertions are not waiting on a sleep. The settle delay is a product option (--settle-ms) that the test exercises: it compares default-delay captures with --settle-ms 0 captures. The test does not use it to time its own assertions. The criterion is about how the browser tests wait, and the guidance excludes settle-delay length from scoring. The claim quotes all three of those files and their shared helpers.ts in full. The unit config runs tests/unit under jsdom, so those tests do not drive a real browser. Only one test drives Playwright directly: the &#39;captures only after the transition settles&#39; test in inspect.int.test.ts. It awaits chromium.launch, page.setContent and page.evaluate, and inside the evaluate it awaits img.decode(). It asserts only after those values have been computed, and it has no fixed sleep. The other tests drive the browser through npm scripts. runNpm resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event, so each test asserts only after the run has finished and its output and exit code exist. The setTimeout in runNpm only sends SIGKILL to a hung child; nothing waits on it before an assertion. previewIsGone is a fetch bounded by AbortSignal.timeout. The only setTimeout in verify.e2e.test.ts is page code that a fault case injects into Scene.tsx. The one fixed wait, page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) at inspect-run.mjs:50, is in the delivered inspect helper, not in a test. It also runs only after waitForStepIndex has polled data-step-index with a timeout, so the step is confirmed by polling first. The review guidance says longer fixed settle delays earn no credit and cause no failure. Nothing in the tests uses an immediately returning call as if it waited. That glob matches exactly three files: inspect.int.test.ts, verify.e2e.test.ts and bootstrap.int.test.ts. helpers.ts is their shared module. The unit config runs tests/unit under jsdom and does not drive a real browser. I quote all four browser files in full, and none of them sleeps for a fixed time or uses an immediately-returning call as a wait. (1) inspect.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits runNpm subprocess runs. The only direct Playwright test, &#39;captures only after the transition settles&#39;, awaits chromium.launch, page.setContent and page.evaluate, and the evaluate awaits img.decode(). It then asserts on pixel counts that have already been computed. The remaining tests assert on PNG files and output that the completed runs produced. (2) verify.e2e.test.ts: every test awaits runNpm and then asserts on the finished process&#39;s output and exit code. previewIsGone is a fetch bounded by AbortSignal.timeout. The only setTimeout in the file is in-page app code that a fault case injects into Scene.tsx. (3) bootstrap.int.test.ts: beforeAll awaits spawnSync and runNpm, and the tests assert on their results and on file contents. (4) helpers.ts: runNpm resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event. Its setTimeout is only a SIGKILL safeguard for a hung child, not a wait before an assertion. Inside the scripts, step changes are awaited by polling: waitForStepIndex calls page.waitForFunction on data-step-index with a timeout. Judge C&#39;s fail rests on page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) at scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs:50. That call is in the delivered inspect helper, not in a test. The helper reaches it only after waitForStepIndex has confirmed the step (line 45), so the test&#39;s step assertions are not waiting on a sleep. The settle delay is a product option (--settle-ms) that the test exercises: it compares default-delay captures with --settle-ms 0 captures. The test does not use it to time its own assertions. The criterion is about how the browser tests wait, and the guidance excludes settle-delay length from scoring. Judge C&#39;s reason therefore does not decide the requirement, and I agree with Judges A and B.","citations":["vitest.browser.config.ts","vitest.config.ts","tests/browser/inspect.int.test.ts","tests/browser/verify.e2e.test.ts","tests/browser/bootstrap.int.test.ts","tests/browser/helpers.ts","scripts/lib/preview.mjs","scripts/lib/inspect-run.mjs"],"evidence":["vitest.browser.config.ts:7 includes only tests/browser/**/*.test.ts; vitest.config.ts:6-7 runs tests/unit under jsdom","tests/browser/inspect.int.test.ts:53-90 uses awaited chromium.launch, setContent, evaluate and img.decode(), with no waitForTimeout or sleep","tests/browser/inspect.int.test.ts:20-34 awaits runNpm runs before any assertion","tests/browser/verify.e2e.test.ts:15-34 and 110-120 assert only after runNpm resolves; line 95&#39;s setTimeout is in-page code injected into Scene.tsx","tests/browser/bootstrap.int.test.ts:22-32 awaits spawnSync and runNpm; the tests then assert on their results","tests/browser/helpers.ts:52-64 runNpm resolves on child &#39;close&#39;; its setTimeout is only a kill safeguard. Please clarify whether the shipped starter must satisfy that quality bar or is an intentionally unstyled authoring stub. This acceptance pass did not run `npm audit`; exact advisory names, affected dependency paths, and applicability are unconfirmed. Observer note and command provenance: `../scratch/acceptance-test/npm-ci-observation.log`. This is not classified as a confirmed product finding."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-cd75a5a9043f2e06 (exploration-log)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":46,"end_line":46,"lines":[{"line":46,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering\\nThe skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. (supersedes the scaling ruling's floor, clipping, and 320 px limit)"},{"line":915,"text":"- Requirement: evolving-scene-presentations, \"Fixed-canvas fit scaling\" (the diagram is \"scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport\"; \"Uniform scaling on resize\"; per-mode fit geometry). Design, \"Stage\" (scale is \"constant within a mode\"; \"scaled by `useFitScale` to the gap between header and footer\"). Design's file layout lists a `MIN_SCALE` constant with no value or semantics. Neither document gives a minimum supported width or allows clipping at a valid viewport."},{"line":916,"text":"- Ruling: The earlier scaling ruling went beyond the approved text in two places, and this ruling replaces them."},{"line":917,"text":" - Replaced: \"`MIN_SCALE` is used and the stage clips\" when the raw fit is below it, and \"320 × 568 is the narrowest supported width\"."},{"line":918,"text":" - For every finite, positive available width and height, in either mode, the scale is exactly the raw fit, `min(availW/DESIGN_W, availH/DESIGN_H)` on that mode's `STAGE_LAYOUT` geometry. This holds even when the result is below `MIN_SCALE`."},{"line":919,"text":" - `MIN_SCALE` is a fallback used only when the measurement is degenerate (zero, negative, or non-finite available width or height, for example before first layout). It is not a lower clamp, so there is no `max(fit, MIN_SCALE)`."},{"line":920,"text":" - Scale stays identical across steps at a fixed viewport and mode. It is recalculated on viewport resize and on mode change, and internal canvas coordinates never change."},{"line":921,"text":" - The checks are unit and component tests:"},{"line":922,"text":" - raw fit is returned exactly at representative viewports, including 320 × 568 and a tiny viewport well below any real device (for example 40 × 40, where the fit is under `MIN_SCALE`);"},{"line":923,"text":" - zero, negative, `NaN`, and `Infinity` inputs return `MIN_SCALE`;"},{"line":924,"text":" - scale is equal across steps and changes on resize and on mode change;"},{"line":925,"text":" - inspection that the transform is a single uniform scale."},{"line":926,"text":" - 320 × 568 is a representative fixture only. It is not a supported-width limit and adds no scope."},{"line":927,"text":"- Rationale: A clamp that engages at a valid positive viewport would let the diagram exceed the available space, which contradicts the spec's \"fit\". The approved text has nothing that permits clipping, and `MIN_SCALE` has no stated semantics, so the narrowest reading consistent with the spec is a degenerate-measurement fallback."},{"line":928,"text":"- Pending decision: None. No approved requirement changes."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-ac30b8b6fb860dc9 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":941,"end_line":979,"lines":[{"line":941,"text":"## Acceptance round 0 — unresolved test-plan fixture ambiguity"},{"line":942,"text":""},{"line":943,"text":"AT-003 asks the tester to inspect entering and departing entities while traversing the committed nine-step reference scene. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's It left the canvas, reflow, and inspector warnings unchanged, because changing them would extend approved scope, and escalated three concrete options to the user. The approved texts conflict: the scaffold must ship zero presentation styling defaults, and the chrome-styling scenario covers generated presentations. This is not classified as a confirmed product finding."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-cd75a5a9043f2e06 (exploration-log)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":46,"end_line":46,"lines":[{"line":46,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering\\nThe skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding\\n- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index\\n- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms\\n\\n### Requirement: Create a new presentation\\nThe skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\n#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created\\n- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index\\n\\n#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style\\n- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look\\n- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist\\n- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable\\n\\n### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Checks run before done\\n- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation\\n- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion\\n\\n#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success\\n- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails\\n- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success\\n\\n### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar\\nEvery generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Builds clean\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated\\n- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Renders without errors\\n- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened\\n- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present\\n- **WHEN** viewing a presentation\\n- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified\\n- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local\\n- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection\\n- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings\\n- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\\n- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome\\n- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible\\n- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":798,"end_line":802,"lines":[{"line":798,"text":"## Where is the GitHub URL for the attribution link?"},{"line":799,"text":"- Requirement: \"Kit attribution\" repository's `origin` remote. It is one exported constant in the kit, and the attribution accepts an override prop."},{"line":801,"text":"- Rationale: It is the only and-scene repository the project knows of. A constant keeps it testable by unit test."},{"line":802,"text":"- Pending decision: None. If the canonical public URL differs, the user changes one constant."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-ac30b8b6fb860dc9 (assumptions-ledger)]"}],"assumption-decisions-and-escalations-proportionate":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":914,"end_line":928,"lines":[{"line":914,"text":"## Does `MIN_SCALE` ever override a valid positive fit? (supersedes the scaling ruling's floor, clipping, and 320 px limit)"},{"line":915,"text":"- Requirement: evolving-scene-presentations, \"Fixed-canvas fit scaling\" (the diagram is \"scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport\"; \"Uniform scaling on resize\"; per-mode fit geometry). Design, \"Stage\" (scale is \"constant within a mode\"; \"scaled by `useFitScale` to the gap between header and footer\"). Design's file layout lists a `MIN_SCALE` constant with no value or semantics. Neither document gives a minimum supported width or allows clipping at a valid viewport."},{"line":916,"text":"- Ruling: The earlier scaling ruling went beyond the approved text in two places, and this ruling replaces them."},{"line":917,"text":" - Replaced: \"`MIN_SCALE` is used and the stage clips\" when the raw fit is below it, and \"320 × 568 is the narrowest supported width\"."},{"line":918,"text":" - For every finite, positive available width and height, in either mode, the scale is exactly the raw fit, `min(availW/DESIGN_W, availH/DESIGN_H)` on that mode's `STAGE_LAYOUT` geometry. This holds even when the result is below `MIN_SCALE`."},{"line":919,"text":" - `MIN_SCALE` is a fallback used only when the measurement is degenerate (zero, negative, or non-finite available width or height, for example before first layout). It is not a lower clamp, so there is no `max(fit, MIN_SCALE)`."},{"line":920,"text":" - Scale stays identical across steps at a fixed viewport and mode. It is recalculated on viewport resize and on mode change, and internal canvas coordinates never change."},{"line":921,"text":" - The checks are unit and component tests:"},{"line":922,"text":" - raw fit is returned exactly at representative viewports, including 320 × 568 and a tiny viewport well below any real device (for example 40 × 40, where the fit is under `MIN_SCALE`);"},{"line":923,"text":" - zero, negative, `NaN`, and `Infinity` inputs return `MIN_SCALE`;"},{"line":924,"text":" - scale is equal across steps and changes on resize and on mode change;"},{"line":925,"text":" - inspection that the transform is a single uniform scale."},{"line":926,"text":" - 320 × 568 is a representative fixture only. It is not a supported-width limit and adds no scope."},{"line":927,"text":"- Rationale: A clamp that engages at a valid positive viewport would let the diagram exceed the available space, which contradicts the spec's \"fit\". The approved text has nothing that permits clipping, and `MIN_SCALE` has no stated semantics, so the narrowest reading consistent with the spec is a degenerate-measurement fallback."},{"line":928,"text":"- Pending decision: None. No approved requirement changes."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-ac30b8b6fb860dc9 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":941,"end_line":979,"lines":[{"line":941,"text":"## Acceptance round 0 — unresolved test-plan fixture ambiguity"},{"line":942,"text":""},{"line":943,"text":"AT-003 asks the tester to inspect entering and departing entities while traversing the committed nine-step reference scene. Please clarify whether AT-003 expects a departure in the reference sample or permits a separate transition fixture. This does not block observing the kit's exit behavior, but the two artifacts describe different fixture expectations."},{"line":944,"text":""},{"line":945,"text":"## Acceptance round 0 — bootstrap starter quality bar"},{"line":946,"text":""},{"line":947,"text":"The bootstrap snapshot registers and links a `Starter` presentation whose presentation-owned CSS is comments only. Please clarify whether the shipped starter must satisfy that quality bar or is an intentionally unstyled authoring stub. Please choose one of the following."},{"line":969,"text":" - Accept about 7–8 px rendered scene text at 390 px wide as the limit of the fixed-canvas design."},{"line":970,"text":" - Approve a phone-specific composition for the sample (a smaller design canvas such as 440 × 380 chosen by viewport, using the existing `designWidth` and `designHeight` props, with entity geometry redone for it)."},{"line":971,"text":" - Approve an inspector advisory warning for small rendered text."},{"line":972,"text":""},{"line":973,"text":"## Acceptance round 1, IMP-001: AXI used a pre-existing `/tmp` browser profile"},{"line":974,"text":"- Question: A mistyped `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_AXI_USER_DATA_DIR` made one diagnostic run use `/tmp/and-scene-axi-profile.APyzZi`, which existed before the round. F-001 remains open at this revision."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-b82a1a510eb6fe57 (final-handoff)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":46,"end_line":46,"lines":[{"line":46,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering\\nThe skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding\\n- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index\\n- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms\\n\\n### Requirement: Create a new presentation\\nThe skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\n#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created\\n- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index\\n\\n#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style\\n- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look\\n- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist\\n- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable\\n\\n### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Checks run before done\\n- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation\\n- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion\\n\\n#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success\\n- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails\\n- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success\\n\\n### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar\\nEvery generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Builds clean\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated\\n- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Renders without errors\\n- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened\\n- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present\\n- **WHEN** viewing a presentation\\n- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified\\n- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local\\n- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection\\n- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings\\n- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\\n- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome\\n- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible\\n- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified
